newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia to invest in tourism.
newsitem.headline: Croatia to invest in tourism.

text.p: Croatia plans to invest more than 100 million kuna on promoting tourism in 1998 and wants to attract one million more tourists, the head of the country's tourist trade association (HTZ) said on Monday.

"Our wishes and forecasts are 5.7 million guests and 34 million overnight stays. This is an ambitious plan...but we have to make an effort to catch the train and make up for all the years we have lost," Marijan Bulat told Vecernji List daily.

Tourism was Croatia's main source of revenue while it was still a republic in federal Yugoslavia, taking in between $4-5 billion a year. But the industry suffered badly during the 1991-95 war with the Serbs.
Before the war, German and Italian tourists were Croatia's most faithful guests and the country is eager to bring them back in large numbers.
"Our plan is to bring 300,000 more German and 200,000 more Italian tourists (in 1998)," Bulat said.
The 1997 season is expected to see a 20 percent rise in overnight stays and tourist spending should rise to 13 to 14 billion kuna from less than 10 billion last year.
The tourist trade accounted for 4-5 percent of Croatian GDP last year and was the country's main currency earner.
